title: Northwest edge capacity sketch - feb 14 2028
content:
Context
- Quick sketch for northwest edge (us-west2 / us-west3 mini-regions). Goal: identify low-cost priming and warm-cache strategies to reduce cold-start tail during promotional surge expected next month. This is a working note — experimenting with mixed static/dynamic priming.

Meeting snapshot (2028-02-14) — quick huddle notes
Attendees: Maya, Rafael, Priya, Ethan, SRE oncall (Lina) joined for 20m
Primary ask from product: support a 3x traffic burst for 12 hours with P95 latency target <= 180ms for hosted tier (A100-backed models).

Observations / current state
- Current northwest edge pool (us-west2) composition: 24 x A100-80GB (prod), 8 x H100-80GB (reserved), 12 x L40s (ephemeral test nodes).
- Average utilization last 7 days: 61% overall. Peak regional overlap with central (us-west1) at 09:00–11:30 PST.
- Cold-start tail (measured from 2028-01-25 to 2028-02-08): 98th percentile extra-ms = 340ms on cold-prefetch routes.
- Idle priming snapshot: 6 prewarmed models (production pinned) but idle cache TTL expires after 45m — too short for promotional pattern.

Quick numbers (sketch):
- Estimated extra tokens during burst: +4.5M tokens/hour -> roughly +70% token/hour vs baseline.
- Batching improvement if primed: expected token-cost drop ~12–18% and P95 latency drop 30–60ms.

Hypotheses to validate
1) Keep a minimal warm pool (2–4 H100-affined instances) and use lightweight cache priming (prefix-only KV prefill) to cut cold tail without large cost increase.
2) Extend idle cache TTL for pinned models to 3 hours for scheduled promos; revert via rollout if not used.
3) Temporarily shift low-criticality background jobs off northwest edge into central region during the burst window to free ephemeral capacity.

Proposed experiment plan (2 days prep, 1-day dry run)
- Day -2: Create priming jobs that replay top-500 recent prompts (by token distribution) as prefix-only prefill into per-model KV caches. Ticket: INFRA-2387. Owner: Rafael.
- Day -1: Increase idle cache TTL for models tagged promo-v1 to 180m via feature-flagged config (console rollout). Ticket: INFRA-2410. Owner: Priya.
- Dry run: schedule a 3h synthetic stress window (weekday, low-business-impact) at midnight PST — observe P95, OOMs, eviction rates. Owner: Ethan + SRE oncall.

Operational safety & rollback plan
- Auto-fallback: if eviction-rate > 6% or GPU mem pressure > 84% for > 10m -> auto-scale down priming: cancel new prefill tasks and reduce TTL back to 45m. Implementation: add a short-circuit in priming controller.
- Manual rollback: runbook section entries to demote promo pool and toggle TTL. Confluence draft: Edge Priming Playbook (linked).

Open risks / questions
- Cost delta unclear: priming H100s for 12 hours could increase committed VM-hours by ~40–60 GPU-hours. Need finance ballpark. Action: Rafael to ping finance (Slack #finance-ops) for quick estimate.
- Model compatibility: some community models behave poorly with aggressive prefix-only KV priming (observed token divergence). Need to mark incompatible models under tag: noskim. Owner: Priya to run compatibility sweep.
- Cross-region traffic spill: if central runs hot, we will see extra cross-region egress and possible rate-limiting. Ask networking to pre-whitelist cross-region flows for the scheduled window. Owner: Maya to loop in NetEng.

Action items (concrete)
- INFRA-2387 (Rafael): implement priming job + add quick metrics pipeline (primed_hits, primed_misses, priming_duration). ETA: 2028-02-16.
- INFRA-2410 (Priya): TTL feature-flag rollout + compatibility sweep for promo-v1 models. ETA: 2028-02-16.
- SRE-check (Ethan + Lina): schedule dry-run and synthetic load script; define SLO violation alert thresholds and oncall playbook. ETA: 2028-02-17.
- Maya: confirm promo window with Growth/Product and notify Sales (impacts demo keys). ETA: 2028-02-15.
- Finance ask: short estimate of incremental GPU-hours and $range for 12-hour H100 priming. Rafael to request.

Notes to self / rough TODOs
- Try reduced prefix priming (50% of token-length) — cheaper and maybe enough.
- Consider temporary reassign of L40 pool to T3 burst tier for non-critical workloads.
- Check autoscaler hysteresis settings — may be too slow for short promos.

Appendix: quick logs & links
- Recent spike timeline (last 2 weeks): attached chart in PR (fleet-ops/pull/482) shows worst-case tail at 2028-02-03 09:05 PST.
- Relevant hooks: /ops/priming-controller, /ops/cache-ttl-config, /sre/oncall-playbooks/edge-surge.md

Conclusion
- This is a sketch; next step is to convert to a 48h action runbook (small, reversible steps) and run a dry rehearsal. If dry-run meets P95 target and no safety triggers, we greenlight promo-week priming.

Unresolved: finance numbers + model compatibility list.
summary: Working sketch for northwest edge priming approach to handle short promotional surges with minimal cost and latency impact. Includes experiment plan, owners, tickets, and safety rollback notes.
